page.layout: One page of verse, set in italic, in stanzas of four lines. Running head and page number at the top. Signature mark at the foot, right. No margin notes.

p.i: Addicta quondam progenies Deo Sic fudit hostes acriorimpios, Victrixque dum Moses fidelis Tendit ad astra manus precantes.
Consulta vera quod Sapientia Semper minorem numine te geris Regina, vinces, hostibusque Sceptra feres metuenda cunctis.
Aeternus orbis nam tibi militat Rector, furentes qui quatit improbos, Virésque vasanas retundit Omne nefas animo moventes.
Qui te benigno lumine respicit, Tutámque praestat: qui vigil excubat, Et fraudis authores recludens Insidias referat latentes.
Infanientum te quibus impetit Turbátque livor Pontificum irritus Omnisque coniurata veros Perdere Christicolas caterva.
Te victus[?] auro nunc parat artifex Miscere mensis toxica regiis Maclare[?], ni tutela Christi Fraude pium caput expediret.
Nunc Iesuites seditionibus Paces Britanni vertere civicis Molitur almas, teq; tentat Legitimis spoliare sceptris.

page.notes: Long s is plain s throughout. u/v spelling corrected where the letter is a consonant (moventes, livor, caterva, civicis). Printed forms kept elsewhere, e.g. authores, Iesuites, teq;. Doubtful readings: "victus" (ligature word, marked [?]), "Maclare" (marked [?]). "Addicta" reads the ct ligature as ct. Signature read as "A. iij" (possibly "A. ij"). Stanza breaks follow the printed four-line groups; verse lines are run together within each stanza.
